html:
The Palikur, who call themselves Parikwene, are an Arawakan people of the lower Oiapoque and Urucauá rivers, on the border of Amapá in Brazil and French Guiana.

A Spanish ship on the coast in 1500 may have recorded their name. They live on the edge of wide wetlands and grow manioc and fish. In colonial times they were caught between the French and Portuguese, and many moved to the Brazilian side. Their language is related to that of the Lokono. Their neighbours include the Cariban Wayana inland. Anthropologists have studied their detailed knowledge of the stars.
sum: The Palikur, who call themselves Parikwene, are an Arawakan people of the lower Oiapoque and Urucauá rivers, on the border of Amapá in Brazil and French Guiana.
